Container.Name: WARHOST
Container.Overview:
WARHOST is a WARNO dedicated server manager for Unraid with mod support, server configuration, and deployment tools. This container runs Eugen's official WARNO dedicated server. The form writes login.ini, variables.ini, and params_for_ai.json for you.
Request a dedicated login and key from eugsupport@eugensystems.com using the email of your EugNet account. Eugen replies with a login and a key. Type both exactly as written. One pair can run five servers. The key stays in this container's Unraid settings and in login.ini inside the settings folder. Do not put it in GitHub, and do not paste it into an issue.
The preset is a 2v2 Conquest server on Jungle Law, from the Red Dragon map pack (Steam Workshop item 3811913066). Max Players, Minimum Players, Team Size, and Combat Rule are on this page because every server needs them set to the map. The map and the workshop mods are under Show more settings, at the bottom of that section. Open Show more settings to pick a different map or mod. Those descriptions list the scenario IDs and the workshop mods. Leave both as they are if you want the Jungle Law preset.
Eugen recommends host networking, and this container uses it, so there is no Docker port mapping. Forward the game port as both TCP and UDP to this Unraid server. You can change the game port later by editing this container; update the router forward to the same number. The server also needs outbound internet access to reach Eugen.
For another server, add a new container from this same template. Change the container name, the game port, and the settings folder. Use the same login and key.
This template was built with AI coding assistants. Humans reviewed what shipped and remain responsible for it.

Write Config From Form, under Show more settings, rewrites the three settings files on every start. Leave it true unless you edit those files by hand. Hand edits are overwritten while it is true. RCON and AI decks are not on this form. Updating the image updates the game files. Update each container after that.

Config.Name: Settings Folder
Config.Description: Folder where this server keeps login.ini, variables.ini, and params_for_ai.json. Unraid creates it if it is missing. Use a different folder for each server, for example /mnt/user/appdata/warno2/settings. login.ini contains your dedicated key. Do not commit this folder to a public repository.

Config.Name: Eugen Login
Config.Description: The login from Eugen's reply, typed exactly as written. It is not your Steam name, and it may not be the email you sent. One login is shared by every server you run with this key, up to five servers.

Config.Name: Eugen Dedicated Key
Config.Description: The dedicated key from the same Eugen reply, typed exactly as written. Unraid hides this box. The key is stored for this container and written to login.ini in the settings folder. Do not put it in GitHub or in a support post. One login and key pair can run five servers.

Config.Name: Public WAN IP
Config.Description: The address Eugen's lobby tells players to connect to. Use your router's public address for internet play. A domain name will not work, and the Unraid server's LAN address is not the address internet players connect to. Forward the game port to Unraid as both TCP and UDP. If you do not know the address, open https://www.whatismyip.com/ from a device on that network.

Config.Name: Game Port
Config.Description: The port this server listens on, and the port WARNO tells players to use. The preset is 10400. You can change it later: on the Docker tab, edit this container, type the new port, and click Apply. Then change the router forward to that same number, both TCP and UDP, aimed at this Unraid server. The port must be free on the Unraid server itself. Host networking does not create a Docker port mapping, so Unraid will not show this port on the Docker page. Each server container needs its own port.

Config.Name: Server Name
Config.Description: Name players see in the WARNO server browser. The preset says Jungle Law 2v2. Change it if you change the map, so players can tell what they are joining. Do not use an equals sign.

Config.Name: Max Players
Config.Description: Total human slots, both teams together. Match the map. A 1v1 map needs 2. A 2v2 needs 4. A 3v3 needs 6. A 4v4 needs 8. A 10v10 needs 20, which is the highest this server accepts. The preset 4 matches Jungle Law, a 2v2. If you pick another map under Show more settings, change this to match.

Config.Name: Minimum Players
Config.Description: How many players must join before the match countdown starts. The preset is 2, so Jungle Law can start with two people even though four slots exist. This cannot be higher than Max Players. Set it equal to Max Players if you want every slot filled before the countdown.

Config.Name: Team Size
Config.Description: Players allowed on one team, not the whole lobby. A 1v1 uses 1, a 2v2 uses 2, a 3v3 uses 3, a 4v4 uses 4, and a 10v10 uses 10. Max Players should be twice this number. The preset 2 matches Jungle Law.

Config.Name: Combat Rule
Config.Description: Type 1 for Destruction or 2 for Conquest. Jungle Law is Conquest, so leave 2. If the scenario ID contains CONQ, use 2. If it contains DEST, use 1. The map list under Show more settings is grouped that way.

Config.Name: Write Config From Form
Config.Description: true rewrites login.ini, variables.ini, and params_for_ai.json from this form every time the container starts. Leave true unless you are editing those files by hand. While this is true, the next start overwrites hand edits. Set false only after those three files already exist in the settings folder.

Config.Name: Workshop Mod Tags
Config.Description: Icons in the WARNO server browser for the kind of mods this server expects. This does not download mods, and it does not decide which map loads. Workshop Mod List is what tells joining players to get a mod. Leave Maps-Scenarios for the Red Dragon map pack: Maps for a map mod, Scenarios for a scenario mod. If you clear Workshop Mod List, you can clear this too. Allowed words, from Eugen: Gameplay, Interface, Maps, Scenarios, Music, and Sound. Join more than one with a hyphen and no spaces, for example Maps-Scenarios. A gameplay mod adds Gameplay, as in Maps-Scenarios-Gameplay. The container stops if this field has a space or a number. A hyphen between words is allowed, as in Maps-Scenarios. A made-up word that is only letters still starts the server, but the browser icon will not match Eugen's list. The Workshop Mod List description gives the tag words for each named mod. This field is optional.

Config.Name: Workshop Mod List
Config.Description:
Workshop mods joining players must already have, or WARNO will ask them to download and enable. This form does not download the mod onto Unraid. It writes the list and starts Eugen's server. Whether that server then downloads the files has not been confirmed. Write each mod as workshopId/version. The version is the Version line in that mod's Config.ini, not a number in the Steam description. Join extra mods with a hyphen and no spaces. Every piece must be digits, a slash, and digits. Clear this whole field for a base-game map with no workshop mod. If a map pack stays filled in while Map is a base-game ID, joining players are still told to download that pack. A conversion is not a map. Keep a scenario ID in the Map field. To require a conversion and a map pack together, join both values with a hyphen only after each Version is the number from that mod's Config.ini.
MODS AND CONVERSIONS. These change the units or the rules. They do not replace the Map field. Players must subscribe in Steam and enable the mod in WARNO. This template does not know their Config.ini Version. After you subscribe, read Version in Config.ini and enter the workshop id, a slash, and that number. Do not copy a version number from the Workshop description. Set Workshop Mod Tags to the words named here, joined with hyphens and no spaces.
Galactic Divide. Workshop id 3595948209. The Workshop page calls it a total conversion. Its page tags are Gameplay, Interface, Sound, Scenarios, and Maps, so Workshop Mod Tags for this mod alone is Gameplay-Interface-Sound-Scenarios-Maps. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3595948209
A World in Flames. Workshop id 3388575848. The Workshop page calls it an overhaul for the modern day. Its page tags are Gameplay and Interface, so Workshop Mod Tags for this mod alone is Gameplay-Interface. If you also require a map pack, add Maps and Scenarios, as in Gameplay-Interface-Maps-Scenarios. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3388575848
MAPS. These add scenarios. Put one scenario ID in the Map field. Red Dragon IDs are listed there. The other map packs are named there without scenario IDs, because their Workshop pages do not publish them. For a map pack alone, leave Workshop Mod Tags at Maps-Scenarios.

Config.Name: Map
Config.Description:
Type the scenario ID, not the name shown in WARNO or on the Workshop page. Jungle Law is rejected. The preset RDPort_JungleLaw_2v2_CONQ is Jungle Law, 2v2, Conquest. Then set Max Players and Team Size to the size in the ID. A 1v1 map needs Max Players 2 and Team Size 1. A 2v2 needs 4 and 2. A 3v3 needs 6 and 3. A 4v4 needs 8 and 4. A 10v10 needs 20 and 10. Combat Rule is 2 when the ID contains CONQ, and 1 when it contains DEST. IDs ending in DUEL, TRAINING, or ASSAULT are special variants of that map; still use the size in the ID. Base-game maps are built into the server: clear Workshop Mod List. A workshop map also needs that mod in Workshop Mod List. Lists go from smallest match to largest.
